title: The 60-second generation budget is enforced consistently
expected: A turn that exceeds LL_GENERATION_BUDGET_S=60 is abandoned at ~60s, every time, with the same outcome
actual: Not enforced consistently. Budget is 60s (GET /api/config -> generationBudgetS=60). Observed: (a) 9-field contract summary ran 237.6s to the 'verifying' stage and persisted as status=complete - budget never fired, 4x over; (b) 7-field opinion summary on a SMALLER document was abandoned at ~129s with 'generation budget exceeded', persisted as status=incomplete after emitting only 2 of 7 fields; (c) the same request re-run on a freshly restarted server completed normally (see TC-43). Cause: turns.py:250 wraps an async generator in 'async with asyncio.timeout(...)' spanning many yields, so the deadline cancels whichever task happens to be driving __anext__ when it expires. Outcome is therefore timing-dependent, not budget-dependent.

title: The backend survives repeated and overlapping Summary turns without crashing
expected: Sequential summary requests complete or fail gracefully; the process stays up
actual: FIXED AND VERIFIED. Originally FATAL: three sequential POST /api/summarize calls crashed the process with 'Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault' - two asyncio.to_thread workers were inside torch simultaneously, one in bge-m3 embed_query (pipeline.py:115) and one in the bge-reranker cross-encoder (rerank.py:107), against process-level model singletons whose lock guarded construction only. Fix: new app/ai/orchestration/retrieval/inference.py holds one process-wide INFERENCE_LOCK, acquired at the leaf torch calls in embedder.embed_documents/embed_query and rerank._score - shared between BOTH models, because the crash was an embed racing a rerank. The lock makes two simultaneous forward passes impossible, which is exactly the condition in the crash stack. Verified post-fix: (a) the same 3 sequential summaries ran 80s/74s/78s with all 7 fields and readyz=200 after each; (b) 4 OVERLAPPING turns - 2 Summary + 2 Ask on the shared models - all completed, same pid, 0 segfaults. 517 backend tests, ruff and mypy --strict all pass. ATTRIBUTION CAVEAT: between the before and after measurements, a separate change by another contributor added background model warm-up at startup (start.py/_start_model_warmup, factory.warm_models). The wall-clock improvement (955s/1021s/crash -> 80s/74s/78s) therefore cannot be attributed to this lock alone. A controlled A/B with the lock disabled was started and then abandoned rather than leave a knowingly crash-prone backend running while the environment was in active use, so the no-crash result rests on the mechanism plus the post-fix concurrency run, not on a completed A/B.

title: A first Ask turn completes rather than deadlocking the server
expected: The first turn in a fresh process returns an answer
actual: FAILED on the code as committed (commit 9ee3e46), then verified fixed. OrchestratedEngine.__init__ created a non-reentrant threading.Lock(); _ask_workflow() acquired it (orchestrated_engine.py:143) and then called _retriever() (line 148), which acquires the same lock (line 116) -> unconditional self-deadlock on the asyncio event-loop thread. Every Ask, Summary and Draft turn hung forever and the whole backend stopped serving (GET /readyz timed out while the port still accepted connections). Reproduced 3/3 times; stack dump attached. Fixed during this run by changing that one line to threading.RLock(), after which the same turn returned a grounded, cited answer in 58s. All AI test cases in this report were executed against the fixed build.

title: Overlapping turns no longer crash the backend (regression test for TC-59)
expected: Several turns dispatched at once leave the process alive, with no segfault
actual: PASS. Two independent samples with the lock in place. (a) Four turns fired simultaneously via curl - 2 Summary + 2 Ask against the shared bge-m3 and cross-encoder: all four done=True, 0 errors, same pid, readyz=200, 0 'Segmentation fault' in the log. (b) The same four fired from the browser via Promise.all: 3 of 4 completed fully, the 4th returned 500 from an unrelated SQLite contention bug (TC-62) - the process still stayed up with 0 segfaults. Before the fix, three SEQUENTIAL summaries were enough to kill it. Note this ran on a build that also has another contributor's startup model warm-up; the lock is what serialises the forward passes, warm-up only pre-loads the weights.

title: Concurrent turns persist without hitting SQLite write contention
expected: Turns running at the same time each persist their record; none fails with a 500
actual: FAIL, intermittent. With four turns in flight, one returned 500 Internal Server Error: sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked (POST /api/conversations/{id}/messages). Not a missing pragma - db.py already sets journal_mode=WAL, busy_timeout=30000, synchronous=NORMAL and a 30s connect timeout. This is writer-vs-writer contention: a turn holds its write transaction across 50-120s of retrieval and generation, and a second writer that must upgrade a deferred read transaction gets SQLITE_BUSY immediately rather than waiting out busy_timeout. Previously masked - the process segfaulted (TC-59) before this could surface. Blocks NFR-5's 10 concurrent users. Fix is structural: keep write transactions short and off the streaming path, or bring forward the M6 move to Postgres.
